target_customer: Consumer gamers on mobile and PC
problem: Unnyhog wanted to unite mobile and PC players in one fantasy MMO with gesture controls.
business_model: Consumer game sales and in-game purchases (not stated by sources)

founders.name: Margarita Belorukova
founders.background_notes: YC page: builds educational video games, uses Unity, Defold, C# and Lua. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A solo-founder cross-platform MMO with gesture controls needs networking, content and client work, which is heavy for one person, though built on standard engines such as Unity.

defensibility.rationale: Game content and mechanics are copyable and no network of players is documented.

market_need_then: No source documents demand for a gesture-controlled cross-platform MMO. The company claims four released games and a latest game, UnnyWorld.

branding.domain_note: unnyhog.com exact match; the site returned an error when fetched.

identity.voice_and_tone: the YC blurb talks of portals to other dimensions and thousands of different lives

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand pages found in the searches.

outcome_analysis: Unnyhog was a one-person game studio in YC W16 that described four released games and an MMO in progress. Dealroom marks it closed in October 2019 and the YC page lists it as inactive, but no article or post-mortem gives a cause. The cause is not public, so failure factors stay empty. Funding appears to have been about 140K USD or less according to databases.
notes: The funding amount rests on a single database (CB Insights, total about 140K); a blog aggregator says 120K across two rounds with a pre-seed in April 2016, unverified. CB Insights lists it as alive while Dealroom lists closure in October 2019, also a single database. The amount is a reported total and round stage and date are unknown. Searches for dated competitors found only unrelated Leap Motion material, so the list is empty. The company site returned a 503.
